description: NarrativeTrace records each traced call, its parameters and its result as log lines through SLF4J, the application's existing logging bridge, and writes a value-free structural trace per test. Install the Gradle plugin (id("ai.narrativetrace")) or depend directly on the ai.narrativetrace:narrativetrace-core Maven artifact and the modules beside it.
rules: Install via the Gradle plugin (id("ai.narrativetrace")); it puts the dependencies on the TEST classpath by default — a traced class under src/main needs the implementation dependencies directly, or scope.set("production") in the plugin DSL.

Pick exactly one of the five attachment mechanisms per project — JDK proxy, Spring, Micronaut, servlet, or the Java agent — per documentation/choosing-an-integration.md; stacking several on one class multiplies frames instead of adding detail.
Values matching the configured redaction rules are replaced with [REDACTED] before any output; keep secrets out of traced parameters and prove redaction with a test asserting on the rendered trace.

Only wrapped or intercepted code appears in a trace; read a run's actual trace output under build/narrativetrace/ before describing what the application did — an unwrapped collaborator leaves no span.
documentation/llms.txt is the curated agent-facing reference; documentation/recipes/ holds complete worked examples, one page per problem.
Running ./gradlew narrativetraceInit --diff previews installing ready-made Claude Code and Codex agent skills (.claude/skills/, .agents/skills/) and a pointer section in AGENTS.md.
